_comment: Why these numbers (the supervisor ignores keys that start with an underscore).
heartbeatTimeoutSec 30: the player writes a beat every 5 s from its first frame, so 30 s is six missed beats; a frozen main thread is seen within half a minute.

heartbeatGraceSec 180: how long a start may take to produce its first beat and to reach app=running (the beat says app=loading, and audio=starting until the sound is up; a running audio clock alone proves nothing, because a Boot that threw leaves the app loading for ever). The player beats from its first frame: on the Mac (Apple M4 Pro, 5 runs with a fresh copy of the build) the first beat came 1.2 s after the process was started, audio=ok 1.3 s, and '[Downbeat] ready' 1.8 s (measurements/day5/boot-to-first-heartbeat.json). The Windows laptop has not been measured. 180 s is 150 times the Mac's first beat, so a laptop that boots tens of times slower still gets through, while a player that never gets there (a hung driver, a build that waits for a shader) is restarted after 3 minutes. It was 90 s when the first beat only came after the sound was up.
audioStallRestartSec 20: the player says audio=stalled (the clock stopped for 3 s) or audio=failed (it gave up after its own 30 s); 20 s more is enough to forgive a device that comes back at once.
backoff.maxRestarts / windowSec / restSec: more than 5 restarts in 10 minutes rest 60 s (a program that crashes at once).

backoff.unstableRuns 3, maxRestSec 600, stableAfterSec 120: when 3 starts in a row never stayed healthy for 2 minutes (an HDMI monitor that is the only sound device is off: every start ends in audio=failed), the rest after each further one doubles, 60, 120, 240, 480 and then 600 s, and one start that stays healthy for 2 minutes puts everything back. 3 is few enough that the thrash is cut within about 3 minutes and many enough that one bad start (a camera held by another program for a moment) is not punished; 600 s is the longest a visitor-less exhibition waits for the device to come back (by arithmetic, not measured: a try takes about 55 s, 30 s for the app to give up on the sound + 20 s + 3 s, so about 520 tries in 8 hours, and one try per 10 minutes is about 50); 120 s is longer than the app's own 30 s boot and the 20 s stall time together, so a start that fails and recovers by itself cannot pass for stable.

processes.name: tracker
processes._comment: heartbeatTimeoutSec 45 for the tracker: its loop beats at least every 2 s, also with no camera (the loop that tries to open it again), so a silence is a read() or an open() that does not return (Media Foundation after a USB unplug). The camera opened in 0.3 s on the Windows laptop with Media Foundation and OPENCV_VIDEOIO_MSMF_ENABLE_HW_TRANSFORMS=0 (tracker/README.md); without that variable it can take tens of seconds (opencv/opencv#17687), so the variable is in the env below and the tracker also sets it itself for -Backend msmf. 45 s is longer than any open that is still alive and short enough that hands are not gone for long. priority aboveNormal: the tracker starts with the above-normal priority class, so that a busy app (the picture) does not starve it on a laptop whose graphics chip and processor share one power budget (the tracker fell to a median of 6 pictures a second); it is stdlib and needs no administrator rights. {trackerPython} has no default: the Python environment is not in the bundle but in %LOCALAPPDATA%/Downbeat/venv (outside a Desktop that OneDrive syncs), and run-supervised.ps1 passes its python.exe with --var trackerPython=.
